one_month_reasoning: In the window: Q3 2026 results, most likely Thursday Oct 22. FCX has not announced the date; it has reported Q3 on Oct 19-23 every year and reported all 2026 quarters on Thursdays, and the Oct 15 date on some calendars is a vendor placeholder. Consensus is $0.74 on guided sales of 750M lb at a $6.00 H2 deck. Copper averaged above that deck, so there is mild upside to the print, offset by the risk of any Grasberg ramp wobble against the 65% H2 target and a cautious first 2027 read. The Section 232 refined-copper tariff is still undecided (the 90-day window lapsed Sep 28). In round 1 I assumed a 'no tariff' headline would squeeze a COMEX premium. That no longer holds: the front-month COMEX-LME spread is already about zero (Oct-26 -$47/t, Nov-26 +$39/t), so the near-term downside from that headline is smaller than I had it. What remains is the slower LME-overhang risk from ~770k short tons in COMEX warehouses, which plays out over quarters, not weeks. I therefore drop the below-spot tilt and centre at about spot (median ~$70.4) with ~14% monthly vol (48%/3.5), plus a hair of extra left tail for the earnings and tariff headlines.

fair_value.method: Three methods on a skeptical $5.90/lb copper deck (below the $6.56 spot) with gold at $4,000/oz, guided 2027 volume of at least 3.72B lb, 31.5% tax and ~38-40% NCI. (1) Forward P/E: 2028E attributable EPS of ~$4.15 x 16x = $66. (2) Attributable FCF yield: 2027E ~$3.19/share at 5% = $64. (3) Rebuilt EV/EBITDA: 2028E EBITDA of $17.6B x 8x, less $4.5B net debt, times a ~62% FCX share = $59. Weighted 0.45/0.35/0.20, the blend is ~$64.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: At the Sep-2027 horizon the stock prices off NTM (2028E) EPS. 2028E EPS $4.15 (full Grasberg, $5.90 Cu) x 16x = $66; cross-check: 2027E EPS $3.89 x 16.5x = $64

Spot is $6.56 and is essentially an LME-level price, since the front-month COMEX premium is about zero (SMM Sep 29). I stay ~10% below spot because of the ICSG 2027 surplus, Goldman's sub-spot 2027 view and ~770k st of COMEX stock that could return to the market if the tariff is dropped. I raised the deck from $5.75 because the tariff-artifact argument no longer applies to spot.
Management's 2027 model gives ~$13B at $5 and ~$20B at $7 (~$3.5B per $1/lb); $13B + 0.9 x $3.5B = $16.15B.
$16.15B - DD&A ~$2.6B - interest ~$0.35B = $13.2B pretax; 31.5% tax = $9.04B; 38% NCI = $5.61B; / 1.44B shares = $3.89. Consensus is $4.16, consistent with a ~$6.05 deck on the same bridge.
Full Grasberg (~4.1B lb) adds ~$1.45B EBITDA, giving $17.6B; after DD&A, 31.5% tax and ~40% NCI (NCI took 52% of H1 2025 net income at full Grasberg, 33% in H1 2026) this is ~$6.0B / 1.44B shares.
2026 guided ETR ~30% (Peru 40%, Indonesia 36%, US 7%). Moved up slightly as the Indonesian mix rises with Grasberg.

H1 2026 $913M of $2,778M = 33% with Grasberg impaired; H1 2025 $1,216M of $2,340M = 52%; 2026 guide ~24% of pretax (~34% of net income). A partial-to-full Grasberg recovery lands in between. Raised from 35%.

At a sub-spot deck I would still pay a discount to FCX's usual high-teens forward multiple because Sep-2027 earnings will include mid-cycle-plus copper, Indonesian jurisdiction risk (IUPK extension, stake step-down to ~37% from 2042) and a pending class action. The spot price is ~17x the $4.16 consensus. Morgan Stanley's $66 EW target implies a similar multiple.

Deduct NCI at its earnings share, not at book: NCI book equity is $12.1B vs $20.1B FCX equity (10-Q), but NCI takes 33-52% of net income. My round-1 ~$24B deduction was far too low.

bear.story: Copper retreats on the LME rather than through a COMEX-to-LME convergence. The Section 232 cathode tariff is formally shelved around the midterms, the ~770k st of COMEX stock leaks back to the world market, and together with the ICSG 2027 surplus this takes copper toward ~$5.00/lb (~$11,000/t). At that price management's model gives ~$13B EBITDA and ~$3.1 attributable EPS. Add a Grasberg setback (PB2/3 chute fix slips past mid-2027, or another wet-muck event) or harsh IUPK extension fiscal terms, and 14x gives ~$44.

base.story: Copper eases to $5.75-6.25. Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027 and nears full rate by year-end; 2027 sales are ~3.7B lb and EPS ~$3.9-4.2. In Sep 2027 the stock prices off ~$4.2-4.4 of 2028E EPS at ~16x, with some multiple compression as the cycle ages. Roughly flat to spot.

bull.story: Copper holds $6.50+ (a supply-deficit view; the tariff may be enacted for 2027, keeping US absorption). Grasberg hits full rate on schedule, 2028E EPS is $5.5-6, and variable returns rise under the 50% payout framework. 17x gives ~$98.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at ~$48 (-32%). At that level the stock is discounting copper near $5/lb (~$13B 2027 EBITDA, ~$3.1 attributable EPS at ~15x) or a real impairment to Grasberg economics: a second block-cave incident, the PB2/3 fix failing, or IUPK extension terms taking a bigger share. That is more than ordinary copper-beta volatility, and it is below the April 2026 guidance-cut low of ~$61 and the lowest current street targets. The supervisor's $47 is essentially the same level.

key_uncertainties: Copper path: spot $6.56 (ATH $6.85 in Sept) is now an LME-level price, not a COMEX artifact; the downside channel is LME weakness from a surplus plus ~770k st of COMEX stock returning if the tariff is dropped
Grasberg ramp: 65% H2-26 to 80% mid-27 to near full end-27, with PB2/3 capped ~60% until the ore-loading fix; it already slipped once (85% to 65%)
Minority leakage: NCI takes ~33-52% of net income depending on Grasberg, which makes attributable earnings much less copper-levered than headline EBITDA suggests
Indonesia jurisdiction: IUPK extension terms and the stake step-down to ~37% from 2042
Insider selling into strength (Chairman ~$25M in Feb 2026; General Counsel $6.3M on Aug 25, 2026) and the pending class action. Neither is thesis-changing alone
reasoning: Round 2 changes. (1) The supervisor showed that my 3.6B lb 2027 volume was below guidance (>=3.72B lb). I now use guidance and carry execution risk in the bear case only. (2) My EV/EBITDA leg deducted ~$24B of NCI. The Q2 8-K shows NCI took 33% of H1 2026 and 52% of H1 2025 net income (I verified $913M/$2,778M and $1,216M/$2,340M), so NCI is worth ~$50B+. I rebuilt the leg to deduct NCI at its ~38% earnings share, used full net debt of $5.3B (including smelter debt), cut its weight to 0.2 and added an attributable FCF-yield leg. (3) I verified the SMM Sep 29 note: front-month COMEX trades at or below LME and the tariff is undecided, so my round-1 'tariff-arbitrage artifact' framing of spot was stale. I raised my deck from $5.75 to $5.90 and re-expressed the bear case as an LME retreat driven by the COMEX stock overhang and the ICSG surplus. (4) Consensus 2027 EPS of $4.16 is confirmed. My own bridge gives $3.89 at $5.90, and the gap is simply the deck. (5) New in-lane checks found no fresh downgrades since MS's April EW/$66 (the Freedom Capital $47 Hold dates from the 2025 incident). Credit is improving (S&P BBB- outlook positive, Moody's Baa3), so there is still no balance-sheet bear case. Net effect: fair value rises from $60 to $64 at a deliberately sub-spot deck; at spot copper the same methods would give ~$75. The skeptic view is that the stock prices spot-like copper at ~17x 2027 consensus with no margin of safety, but the Grasberg volume ramp (+20% Cu, +50% Au) is a real idiosyncratic offset. I set the 12-month median at ~$68.5 (was ~$67): slightly below spot, lognormal sigma ~0.44 with a modestly fattened left tail. Scenario mean is ~$69.5. The 1-month ladder is recentred at spot because the near-term tariff-headline downside I assumed is mostly gone. Research this round was limited to one filing fetch, one article fetch and two searches.
